title.narrative: Output 2.2. Increased capacity of the member States to apply international labour standards

description.narrative:
CEACR Observation on C 100: "The Committee notes with satisfaction that, in the new Labour Law adopted on 2 June 2021, the definition of "salary" includes the "basic salary, allowances, additional wages and vacation pay and bonuses" (section 101.1) and that, pursuant to section 102.1.1, the salary of employees "performing jobs of equal value shall be the same". In addition, the Committee welcomes the explicit prohibition of salary discrimination on the basis of sex or other grounds (section 102.1.4.)."
CEACR Observation on C 111: The Committee notes that the new Labour Law was adopted on 2 June 2021 and will enter into force on 1 January 2022. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Labour Law: (1) defines and prohibits both direct and indirect discrimination; (2) limits the exceptions to discrimination to the inherent requirements of the work or duty performed and special protective measures; (3) broadens significantly the list of prohibited grounds of discrimination including "political opinion" and many additional grounds such as "ethnicity", "language", "age", "marital status", "trade union membership", "health status", "pregnancy or childbirth", "sexual orientation", "sexual expression", "disability" and "appearance" etc. The Office started providing technical assistance with the revision of the Labour Law (1999) in 2010, in fact 2 years before the revision process formally got under way. The Office provided support with capacity-building to the constituencies separately and collectively on the functions and basic concepts of labour law in the context of contemporary labour market governance; relevant international labour standards, including pending comments of the supervisory bodies; and principles of labour relations and dispute settlement. Assistance took the form of periodical seminars convened between 2012 and 2019; virtual advisory sessions with MPs in 2020; two technical memoranda on draft revisions of the Labour Law; consultancies, including by constituents from other countries in the region; and a tripartite study tour (to Japan).

description.narrative: Mongolia ratified C.167 in January 2020 and it is registered in November 2020. The Convention will enter into force for Mongolia on 05 Nov 2021. ILO has provided support to the Government and social partners on ratification of the convention. This includes legal comparative analysis and situational analysis. However, all these supports were provided in previous biennia.

description.narrative: The Office received all article 22 reports on Conventions nos. 87, C 98, C 103, C 144, C 155, C 176 and the MLC due by the deadline. The Office organized a tailor-made workshop for Mongolia on training on ILS reporting from 14 May to 30 November 2021. The purpose of the training was to understand better the CEACR's comments, and to prepare quality reports to respond the requests. Members of the National Tripartite Sub-Committee on the Application of ILO Conventions and Recommendations including representatives of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection , the Mongolian Employers' Federation , the Confederation of Mongolian Trade Unions , the Mongolian Maritime Administration , the General Agency for Social Insurance , the General Agency for Labour and Social Welfare Services , the General Agency for Specialized Inspection , the Ministry of Construction and Urban Development , the Ministry of Mining and Heavy Industry and other relevant organizations participated in the training on Reporting. A total of six training sessions were held on 4 May 2021 on various topics such as Introduction to ILO Supervisory Mechanism and the Tripartite Consultation Convention C144; Application and reporting on C87 and C98; Application and reporting of C103 and C183 ; Application and reporting of C155 and C176; Application and reporting of C167; Application and reporting of C138 and C182 ; and- Application and reporting of C29 and C105.
